records.summary: Tambo installs and verifies the knowledge-tool stack from a reviewable plan. The transition retains the caboodle command and existing plan/state paths; publication and installed verification remain separate.

records.subject: http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/doc/tambo/docs%2Fbook%2Fsrc%2Farchitecture.md
records.summary: The architecture separates plan, apply and verify. Guided intended-use answers become reviewable plan data and executable reader-path contracts rather than implicit permission to install.

records.subject: http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/code/tambo/src%2Fmain.rs
records.summary: The Clap command tree defines quickstart, plan, apply, verify and doctor, with explicit plan/state paths and opt-in remote credential provisioning.

properties.publicName: tambo and compatible caboodle command tree

records.subject: http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/code/tambo/src%2Fmodel.rs
records.summary: The serialized Plan schema defines profiles, ordered tools, optional shares and destination database, intended-use contracts and host exclusions. Unknown plan fields are rejected.

records.subject: http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/code/tambo/src%2Fadapter.rs
records.summary: The Adapter trait separates desired version, installation, version read-back and functional verification. Built-in adapters integrate the selected stack tools; package adapters may bind verification to PATH executables.

records.subject: http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/code/tambo/Cargo.toml
records.summary: The package and primary command are tambo, while the Rust library import name remains caboodle and a legacy caboodle binary is explicitly declared for compatibility.
